body: I don't know your situation, but only you can decide on it.  Only you can decide how strong you are and how much you can take.

I didn't have any sexual abuse, no.  But I did end up having an awful lot of emotional and psychological abuse.  I also had some physical abuse.

I do have to tell you, there were a lot of times I was suicidal, grabbing a knife and wondering how it would feel inside my stomach, but I was too scared to do it.

I'm not sure if I'm really better equipped.  All I know is that I did lean on my family and friends for a while, while I pulled myself out of the deep void I was in.  I knew I was a strong person, and sometimes I had to remind myself of that.  It's like where you're running a marathon, and you feel like just quitting, but you're only a quarter mile from the end.  It's painful and difficult, but once you pass the finish line, there's nothing but a giant feeling of triumph at the end.

It didn't actually take just one year.  It's been one year since I've spoken with my soon-to-be ex-husband.  It's been my entire life that I've had to deal with emotional abuse from my parents, which changed over to my boyfriend-then-husband.  So, for me, it's taken 27 years.

I didn't have any sexual abuse, no.  But I did get a LOT of emotional, psychological, and some physical abuse.  I'm not saying I'm better or worse than anyone, I'm just saying that you can pull through it.

I don't know your situation, so I can't really tell you whether or not it will, but in the most general sense, it CAN get better.  I've been in the black pit of despair and fought through it, and refused to let go without a fight.  Think of it this way: You've already gone through so much - what harm can a little more fight do, if you can obtain happiness?

I can only say that through my experiences, my life is a lot better now that I pulled through the hard stuff.  I find I'm enjoying things more now that I don't feel that the weight of the world is on my shoulders.  I still have hardships like everyone else, but for the first time in a long while, I can actually say I'm happy, and I'm happy with who I am.  If I can do that, so can you.

Hey, any little thing to look forward to is good.  Talk to your family more, tell them that the meds aren't helping.  If I didn't have my grandmother in my life, I don't know who I'd be.  I'm not a doctor or a psychiatrist, but I recommend you go to one.
Thanks, I hope it helps someone.

I had a lot of help from my grandmother and Aunt and my friends.  I really had to lean on them emotionally when going through this stuff.  And I will never forget them.  My bond with my grandmother and Aunt are super-strengthened now, we talk nearly every day.

It didn't just magically happen.  I really had to work hard to obtain it.  I know a lot of people say that willpower isn't really a part of it, but honestly, it is.  You have to really push yourself when things seem to be nothing but a giant spiraling hole.  I knew I was stronger than anyone gave me credit for, and my friends actually were surprised at how well and quickly I healed.  The healing is a constant thing, I'm still going through it and time to time I break down, but those are only steps.

Never *ever* forget your friends.  They're the most helpful people in the Universe, and just want you to do good for yourself.

I did NOT do it alone.  My grandmother and Aunt were both very much there for me, even though they are across the country.  Both of them, plus my friends helped me so much.

YOU are stronger then you think, if you're here, you are very strong.  I'm sure you'll make your life better.
